signal: Conduktor raised a $30M Series B to fund US expansion and grow its US team

email.body1:
Steve, saw Conduktor closed its $30M Series B and is leaning hard into US expansion.

New market, new team, and the signal-to-action gap usually widens fast: in-market accounts surface faster than reps can research, write, and follow up. Our AI SDR handles that autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount, 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Conduktor off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Steve, quick follow-up for Conduktor.

Post-raise, the US number tends to climb faster than RevOps can wire up clean signal-to-meeting routing, so the gap shows up late in the quarter when it is hardest to fix.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Conduktor needs to hit target this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Steve, last bit of proof for Conduktor.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Conduktor's reply rate likely compares to other Series-B startups. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Steve, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling US pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. The post-raise stretch is its own kind of busy, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your RevOps motion? I will tailor it to Conduktor either way.
